free.title: JAMAICA BAY WILDLIFE REFUGE
free.caption:
OUTDOORS · JAMAICA BAY WILDLIFE REFUGE

Free bird sanctuary in Queens that most Manhattanites have never set foot in.

Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge is 9,000+ acres of salt marsh and ponds run by the National Park Service, and it's completely free to walk. Egrets and herons work the shoreline daily, and over 330 bird species have been logged here, more than almost anywhere else in the city.

Pick up a free permit at the visitor center (Friday through Monday, 10am-4pm), then walk the flat 1.5-mile West Pond loop. Bring binoculars if you have them, the best sightings are across open water and the refuge doesn't rent any.

Send this to whoever keeps saying they want to get outside more.

food.title: GRAND ARMY PLAZA GREENMARKET
food.caption:
FOOD · GRAND ARMY PLAZA GREENMARKET

Brooklyn's other Saturday farmers market, and it's a fraction of the Union Square crowd.

Every Saturday, about 40 farms from the Hudson Valley and Long Island set up at the Prospect Park entrance for the Grand Army Plaza Greenmarket, one of GrowNYC's original markets. Vegetables, cheese, bread and honey change with the season, and there's rarely a line.

Show up before 10am if you want the good radishes and greens, they go fast. Most stands take cards, but bring a tote for the walk back.

It sits right at the park entrance, so pair it with a lap around the Long Meadow.

Send this to the person who complains about Union Square but still hasn't tried this one.

art.title: ARTE MUSEUM NEW YORK
art.caption:
ART · ARTE MUSEUM NEW YORK

Chelsea's immersive art museum just turned one, and tickets are as low as $29.99 this month.

ARTE MUSEUM packs a dozen-plus rooms of projected forests, tides and light into 61 Chelsea Piers, each paired with its own scent and soundscape so it reads more like a walk through nature than a screen. The anniversary pricing runs through September, well under the usual $45-60 range.

Book a timed slot if you're going on a weekend; mornings move faster and the rooms photograph better without a crowd in frame. End at ARTE CAFE, where the table itself becomes part of the art.

Send this to whoever's been looking for an indoor date idea.
